To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Fas ligand-induced apoptosis of periarticular knee tenocytes was more pronounced in osteoarthritic (OA) tendons than in controls.

periarticular tenocyte cultures from osteoarthritis patients were more susceptible to FAS-ligand induced apoptosis than controls, and that the apoptosis inhibiting effect of tumor necrosis factor-alpha was less pronounced in osteoarthritis tenocytes than in control tenocytes.
periarticular tenocyte apoptosis is increased in knee OA and that TNF-α inhibits apoptosis in these cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of Fas and TNF in the pathogenesis of knee osteoarthritis and tendinosis.
the role of Fas ligand/Fas and TNF-α induced apoptosis in degenerative changes in periarticular tendons.
the molecular mechanisms of apoptosis and its inhibition in the pathogenesis of knee osteoarthritis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Fas ligand-induced apoptosis is a major mechanism of cell death in periarticular OA tenocytes.
Fas ligand-induced apoptosis of periarticular knee OA tenocytes is more susceptible than that of control tenocytes.
Fas and Fas ligand play an important role in the pathogenesis of OA and that Fas ligand may be a potential therapeutic target for this disorder.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Fas is overexpressed in OA tenocytes, which may be due to the increased expression of the Fas receptor.
the expression and function of the Fas/FasL system is altered in periarticular OA tenocytes.
Fas ligand induces apoptosis in OA tenocyte and TNF-α reduces apoptosis induced by Fas ligand.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the periarticular tendon cells of patients with knee joint OA are more susceptible to FASL induced apoptosis and that this increased sensitivity is due to increased Fas expression.
Fas ligand is expressed in tendon and that it is involved in apoptosis.
the Fas ligated-induced apoptosis is higher in OA tenocytes compared to non-OA tenocytes.
